A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work. All 18 pages of v3 and 19 pages of v4, including appendices, equations, tables, and figures, support comparison after matching relocated material.

before.justification: V3 reports original controlled pre-training experiments on contamination, scaling, forgetting, and weight decay, including GPT-3 and OLMo experiments and appendix controls.

after.justification: V4 retains these original experiments and adds analysis of benchmark overlap with FineWeb-Edu and a normalized comparison of OLMo forgetting curves.

M1.justification: The model architectures, contamination-insertion procedure, benchmark deduplication, evaluation approach, and AdamW training framework remain unchanged. The new corpus audit and curve comparison are supplementary analyses.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same seven benchmarks and pre-training corpora. The new overlap audit examines retained datasets. OLMo-1B was already evaluated in v3, including its appendix.

E2.justification: The evaluated models and clean/holdout comparisons are retained. V4 combines previously reported OLMo-1B and OLMo-7B results in Figure 3; it does not introduce a new comparison method. Newly cited studies are not evaluated as baselines.

E3.justification: New Appendix A.6 specifies normalized longest-common-substring analysis of 44,000 questions against the entire 100B-token corpus, comparing single-best and top-ten matches. Figure 3 adds baseline centering and 5.9-fold rescaling of the OLMo-1B curve. These are additional analysis protocols; existing training protocols are otherwise retained.

E4.justification: V4 adds a substantial validity audit of pre-existing benchmark contamination: Appendix A.6 and Figures 7–8 examine overlap across benchmarks, repeated matches, and an ARC-Easy case distinguishing textual overlap from answer leakage. Section 4.3 also adds model-size-normalized forgetting analysis. V3 only compared the OLMo models qualitatively.

E5.justification: Bootstrapped 90% confidence intervals remain the principal experimental uncertainty reporting, and the filtering validation retains its 95% intervals. No new run counts, seeds, or statistical estimation procedures are reported. Some plotted interval values change, which affects results rather than reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the main OLMo summaries remain unchanged, but some plotted values are revised: Figure 2(c)'s 4x accuracy difference changes from approximately +0.56 to -0.39 percentage points. V4 additionally reports alignment after 5.9-fold OLMo rescaling and overlap concentrated in BoolQ, MMLU, and ARC-Easy, usually with fewer than ten high-overlap occurrences.

T1.justification: Equations 1–4, Proposition 1, and its proof are retained, with the proof moving from Appendix A.5 to A.8. The exponential-moving-average remark adds interpretation and attribution without changing the derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the central claims about joint scaling, forgetting contamination with sufficient subsequent data, and cumulative weight decay as a guide to forgetting. The additional analyses support these claims without redefining the main contribution.

C2.justification: Appendix A.6 newly explains that experiments estimate the effect of additional copies when pre-existing contamination exists, and that textual overlap need not disclose the correct answer. V4 also adds a proportional model-size/token interpretation, sharper stability and data-attribution implications, and an explicit limitation concerning validation beyond 7B parameters.

D1.justification: V4 adds a specific cumulative-weight-decay notebook link, exact OLMo parameter counts, and disclosure that FineWeb-Edu was used without decontamination. Reported OLMo-7B resources change from three weeks on eight H100s to six weeks on four H100s; this does not establish that experiments were rerun. Existing repository access was already documented in v3.

R1.justification: V4 adds Kocyigit et al. on translation contamination, Muennighoff et al. on data-constrained training, Wang and Aitchison on AdamW, and Singh et al. for overlap measurement. These modestly extend positioning; numerous other reference changes update publication metadata for existing works.

P1.justification: Most prose and section ordering remain recognizable. V4 revises portions of Sections 4.3, 5.3, and the discussion, adds Takeaways, Limitations, and an Impact Statement, standardizes accuracy-difference terminology, and corrects some epoch/Chinchilla wording and citation formatting.

P2.justification: The main text and references change from a single-column manuscript to a two-column conference layout. Figure 3 is rebuilt as an OLMo overlay, while the individual plots remain in Appendix Figures 9–10. Two overlap figures are added, and numerous plot labels, captions, sizing, and placements change.

improvement.justification: V4 improves transparency through the corpus-overlap audit and its explanation of what pre-existing contamination means for the experiments. The normalized OLMo comparison, clearer limitations, and notebook link also help readers assess and reproduce the work. These are useful supporting gains; the core experiments and theory remain largely unchanged, and textual overlap still does not establish answer leakage.
